rows.source_population: 14 family caregivers caring at home for older adults (aged >= 60 years) with stroke in Iran (translated quote from Participant 10 describing sudden neurological changes in an older woman)
rows.family_population: spouse carer describing a 72-year-old wife on daily blood pressure pills whose speech suddenly became slurred at breakfast 20 minutes ago
rows.note: Both involve family caregivers recognizing sudden slurred speech in an older female adult ('her speech becomes slurred' inflected to past tense 'her speech became slurred'), adapted from translated Persian interviews with post-stroke home caregivers in Iran to an English-speaking spouse witnessing hyperacute stroke onset.

rows.source_population: 9 UK adults aged 26-72 years (4 women, 5 men) interviewed after hospital admission for symptomatic pulmonary embolism (Participant 2F quote)
rows.family_population: 57-year-old adult 10 days after right collarbone surgery who suddenly developed inspiratory chest pain while sitting still today
rows.note: Same adult symptomatic pulmonary embolism population (cohort ages 26-72 years); verbatim patient phrase 'a pain in the chest' used directly.

rows.source_population: 22 English-speaking US patients aged 12-72 years (21 adults; 36.4% male; 81.8% non-Hispanic White, 18.2% racial/ethnic minority) diagnosed with nonsegmental vitiligo affecting the hands and body
rows.family_population: 24-year-old man with dark brown skin having smooth chalk-white patches spreading on the backs of both hands over 6 months
rows.note: Same adult bilateral-hand nonsegmental vitiligo presentation ('white patches' on both hands used verbatim), but the source sample was predominantly female (63.6%) and non-Hispanic White (81.8%) with individual quote speaker skin tone unspecified whereas the family specifies a 24-year-old man with dark brown skin.

rows.source_population: 12 completely edentulous older adults aged 65-87 years wearing conventional complete dentures in Montreal, Canada (quote from Participant 7, aged 78)
rows.family_population: 72-year-old adult with a loose upper full denture for 3 weeks rubbing a painful raw sore on the roof of the mouth
rows.note: Same older-adult (aged 65-87 years) conventional complete-denture population experiencing prosthesis instability and oral mucosal trauma; verbatim patient adjective 'loose' used directly.

rows.source_population: 15 adults newly diagnosed with Graves' disease (12 women [80%], 3 men; aged 29-74 years) interviewed at a secondary referral center in Sweden (Participant 11 quote)
rows.family_population: 29-year-old woman with 7 kg weight loss in 3 months despite big meals, bilateral hand trembling, and resting pulse of 108 beats per minute
rows.note: Same adult female hyperthyroid / Graves' disease population (cohort ages 29-74 years, 80% women); verbatim patient symptom term 'trembling' used directly.

rows.source_population: 15 adults newly diagnosed with Graves' disease (12 women [80%], 3 men; aged 29-74 years) interviewed on initial symptom interpretation in Sweden
rows.family_population: 29-year-old woman with 7 kg weight loss in 3 months despite big meals, bilateral hand trembling, and resting pulse of 108 beats per minute
rows.note: Same adult female hyperthyroid / Graves' disease population questioning whether hypermetabolic symptoms stemmed from life stressors; adapted into present-tense belief clause 'and I think it's stress'.

rows.source_population: 12 adults aged 19-64 years (illness duration >= 6 months, mean onset 21.75 years) living with body dysmorphic disorder interviewed in Australia
rows.family_population: 23-year-old adult with 6 months of getting stuck in 4-hour daily mirror-checking routines focused on the nose keeping them home from work
rows.note: Same adult body dysmorphic disorder population (ages 19-64 years, duration >= 6 months) reporting mirror-checking compulsions; verbatim phrase 'stuck in checking routines' used directly.

rows.source_population: 12 adults aged 22-50 years (70% full-time employed) with chronic insomnia disorder experiencing difficulty initiating sleep
rows.family_population: 48-year-old adult with 5 months of nightly bedtime racing thoughts and taking 2 hours to fall asleep
rows.note: Same adult chronic sleep-onset insomnia population (ages 22-50 years); verbatim patient phrase 'having racing thoughts' used directly.

rows.source_population: 12 adults aged 22-50 years with chronic insomnia disorder reporting prolonged baseline sleep-onset latency (mean 101 minutes)
rows.family_population: 48-year-old adult with 5 months of nightly bedtime racing thoughts and taking 2 hours to fall asleep
rows.note: Same adult chronic sleep-onset insomnia population (ages 22-50 years, baseline mean 101 minutes to fall asleep); verbatim phrase 'to fall asleep' used directly.

rows.expression: and I think it's work stress
rows.source_population: 12 adults aged 22-50 years (70% full-time employed) with chronic insomnia disorder describing presleep cognitive barriers
rows.family_population: 48-year-old adult with 5 months of nightly bedtime racing thoughts and taking 2 hours to fall asleep
rows.note: Same adult employed chronic sleep-onset insomnia population describing bedtime wakefulness driven by racing thoughts 'about work', adapted into present-tense belief clause 'and I think it's work stress'.

rows.expression: and I think stress caused it
rows.source_population: 14 young women diagnosed with premature ovarian insufficiency (aged 26-39 years at assessment) interviewed in Persian in Iran
rows.family_population: 25-year-old English-speaking woman with previously regular 28-day periods whose last period started 7 months ago
rows.note: Same young-adult female secondary-amenorrhea / ovarian-insufficiency domain attributing amenorrhea to stress ('some women believed stress caused their POI'), adapted from diagnosed Persian-speaking participants aged 26-39 years in Iran to an undiagnosed 25-year-old English speaker ('and I think stress caused it').

rows.source_population: 15 first-time mothers of infants/toddlers aged <= 24 months in Australia with De Quervain's tendinosis / thumb-side wrist pain during infant care (Participant P3 quote)
rows.family_population: adult daily caregiver of a 4-month-old baby with 3 weeks of sharp thumb-side right wrist pain when picking up the baby
rows.note: Same infant-care De Quervain's thumb-side wrist tendinopathy population (4-month-old infant within <= 24 months); verbatim patient phrase 'picking up my baby' used directly.

rows.source_population: 17 adults (ages 18-75 years, mean 33.1 years) and 4 adolescents (ages 12-17 years) in the US with clinician-confirmed eosinophilic esophagitis interviewed on dysphagia symptoms
rows.family_population: 63-year-old adult who swallows water and soup easily with solid meat getting stuck behind the breastbone at every dinner for 6 weeks
rows.note: Same adult esophageal solid-food dysphagia symptom domain ('getting stuck' used verbatim, cohort ages up to 75 years), adapted from a predominantly younger eosinophilic esophagitis cohort (adult mean age 33.1 years, 'food getting stuck in the throat') to a 63-year-old adult with progressive retrosternal solid-meat dysphagia.

rows.source_population: 17 symptomatic menopausal / perimenopausal women in the UK interviewed on vasomotor symptoms and treatment preferences
rows.family_population: 50-year-old woman sleeping in a cool bedroom waking 4 times nightly for 3 months soaked from hot flushes and night sweats
rows.note: Same symptomatic perimenopausal / menopausal female vasomotor population; verbatim symptom pair 'hot flushes and night sweats' used directly.

rows.source_population: 13 outpatients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease using inhalers recruited from two Australian tertiary hospital respiratory clinics (quote from Cynthia, P13)
rows.family_population: 68-year-old adult with a 35-year smoking history on a daily inhaler experiencing acute severe breathlessness ('can't catch my breath') sitting upright
rows.note: Same chronic smoking-related airway disease / inhaler-user population; patient phrase 'can’t catch my breath' (matching core entry 'can't catch my breath' in dialect_lexicon_20261109.json) normalized to ASCII apostrophe.

rows.source_population: 73-year-old woman presenting to a US emergency department (Mayo Clinic, Minnesota) with syncope and a history of dizzy spells ultimately attributed to a left atrial myxoma
rows.family_population: spouse describing a 42-year-old male US factory worker with heavy sweating, a brief dizzy spell, and a 105 F oral temperature after 4 hours on a hot factory floor
rows.note: Both are US emergency clinical presentations using colloquial 'dizzy spell(s)' (matching core entry 'spell' in dialect_lexicon_20261109.json), adapted from a 73-year-old woman with cardiac syncope and 'dizzy spells' to singular 'dizzy spell' in a 42-year-old factory worker with exertional hyperthermia.

rows.source_population: English speakers using colloquial/dialect adjective 'swimmy' for dizziness (Wiktionary lexical entry 'swimmy', Adjective sense 1; attests lexical sense only)
rows.family_population: 49-year-old colloquial English speaker with 4 months of brief swimmy-headed attacks, left-ear roaring, and muffled left-ear hearing despite 6 weeks of doctor-prescribed medication
rows.note: Wiktionary dictionary sense ('Dizzy; swirling or moving as if seen in a daze', matching core entry 'swimmy headed / my head feels swimmy' in dialect_lexicon_20261109.json) attests general lexical meaning rather than an otoneurologic patient cohort; combined into 'swimmy headed'.

rows.source_population: 96-year-old Australian man with insulin-treated type 2 diabetes and metastatic insulinoma referred to endocrinology in Sydney for recurrent carbohydrate-relieved hypoglycemic 'funny turns'
rows.family_population: 71-year-old Australian English speaker with 4 late-afternoon episodes of shaking and sweating ('funny turns') over 3 weeks relieved by eating crackers
rows.note: Same older-adult Australian endocrine clinical setting reporting recurrent carbohydrate-relieved hypoglycemic 'funny turns' verbatim (matching core entry 'a funny turn' in dialect_lexicon_20261109.json), adapted from a 96-year-old man with longstanding diabetes and metastatic insulinoma to an undiagnosed 71-year-old outpatient.
